title: A returning Google sign-in that is not admitted can follow the redirect to the whitelist page
steps: S1: From the repo root at the commit under test: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/security-headers.test.mjs
S2: Read the line for the test whose name starts with 'a refused Google sign-in may end at the whitelist page'.
expect: That test reports ok: with BETA_GATE=on and a whitelist page on another origin, GET /login answers a content-security-policy whose form-action is 'self' accounts.google.com github.com plus that origin (pre-fix: no third origin, so the browser blocked the 303 from /signin/google/callback to the whitelist page and nothing happened on screen).
evidence: Measured 07/10/2026 on cowork.tracy.ai: console 'Sending form data to .../signin/google?next=... violates ... form-action self accounts.google.com github.com. The request has been blocked.' on the second Google sign-in of an address that was not admitted.
fence: apps/tracy-web/src/lib/security-headers.js: hardenPage adds the whitelist origin set by app.js to form-action.

tests: a refused Google sign-in may end at the whitelist page
